overview: I received my M.D. degree from the Federal University of Rio Grande do Sul in Brazil, followed by residency in Internal Medicine at the same institution. I moved to the United States with my husband in 1986 to become a Research Fellow at the National Institutes of Health in Bethesda, Maryland, for 2 years. We then moved to Boston, where I continued working as a fellow at Harvard Medical School. In 1993, we relocated to Birmingham, Alabama. I completed a residency in Pathology and a fellowship in Hematopathology at UAB and am Board certified in Anatomic and Clinical Pathology, with subspecialties in Hematology and Transfusion Medicine/Blood Banking. I am Professor of Pathology at UAB, serving medical director of Transfusion Services. I spent my time doing patient care, teaching, clinical research and administrative duties. In the clinical arena, I am particularly interested in improving appropriateness of utilization of blood products and laboratory tests. I thoroughly enjoy giving lectures locally and in other institutions on these topics and the role of the clinical pathologist in decreasing diagnostic error. Finally, UAB is a pioneer in Patient Blood Management through a collaboration between the Transfusion Services, clinicians and hospital administration since 2007.
